paper_metadata.title: Origin of localizing creep damage in Ni-based single crystal superalloys pre-strained at room temperature

evidence.quote: This work investigates mechanisms of irregular microstructure evolution and creep damage localization induced by the prior room-temperature plastic deformation applied to Ni-based single crystal superalloys, AM1 and CMSX-4 Plus
Chemical composition of alloys in weight % (Ni bal.).
Two Ni-based SX superalloys, 1st generation AM1 and 3rd generation CMSX-4 Plus, were selected for this study.

AM1 SX bars having a 14 mm diameter were produced by Bridgman directionally solidifying precision casting and they were solution heat treated at 1300 °C for 3 h and cooled down at 5 K/s (300 K/min) in Safran Aircraft Engines foundry.
Chemical composition of alloys in weight % (Ni bal.).
As-cast CMSX-4 Plus SX plate having a 10 mm thickness was produced by the same Bridgman casting and supplied by Safran Tech.

attributes.morphology: slight evolution in 45°/225° directions with stronger tendency of P-type rafting (0°/180°) inside the band

evidence.section: 3.2 γ′ precipitate size and morphologies after the heat treatments
evidence.quote: In the case of AM1-PD-A1 (Fig. 6 (c)), the γ ′ precipitates showed slight evolution in 45 ◦ /225 ◦ directions with stronger tendency of a P-type γ ′ -rafting (0 ◦ /180 ◦ ).

attributes.morphology: elongated in both [001] and [010] directions equally

evidence.quote: The rose diagram of AM1-PD-A1A2 in Fig. 6 (d) shows an oval with 45 ◦ rotation (135 ◦ /315 ◦ directions) which is the parallel direction to the microstructure coarsened band.

evidence.quote: Because the first stage HT was at a higher temperature 1165 ◦ C and for a longer duration 6 h, cubic γ ′ precipitate size of CMSX-4 Plus (500 – 600 nm) is much larger than that of AM1 (350 – 450 nm).

phases_and_microstructures.name: L12 γ′ precipitates

attributes.morphology: rectangular, coarsening and coalescence of nearby precipitates

evidence.section: 3.2 γ′ precipitate size and morphologies after the heat treatments
evidence.quote: the small increase of the γ ′ size during the secondary HT was just a consequence of increasing γ ′ phase volume fraction (from 52 % to 65 – 70 % [ 32 ])

evidence.quote: The thickness of the bands has a range of 2 – 20 μ m for both AM1-PD-A1 and 4P-PD-A1 specimens, and it can be up to 250 μ m for AM1-HT-PD-A1 specimen.

attributes.morphology: paired dislocations in a/2<110>{111} slip systems

evidence.section: 3.3 STEM multi-scale characterization of the microstructure
evidence.quote: After the first stage HT, complex dislocation arrangements are observed mainly at the γ / γ ′ interfaces.

evidence.section: 3.3 STEM multi-scale characterization of the microstructure
evidence.quote: Interfacial dislocations and 60 ◦ type matrix dislocations are similar to those reported for very early primary creep stage of Ni-based SX superalloys

phases_and_microstructures.name: dislocation groove
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: pre-deformed and annealed at 1100 °C for 5 h

evidence.section: 3.2 γ′ precipitate size and morphologies after the heat treatments
evidence.quote: associated with dislocation grooves exposed by etching and observed at the γ / γ ′ interface

evidence.section: 3.1 Pre-deformation of Ni-based SX superalloy specimens
evidence.quote: In the as-solutioned state, AM1 has higher yield strength at RT compared to that of CMSX-4 Plus

Dislocation climb similar to what occurs during the high-temperature low-stress creep is the main mechanism of the microstructure evolution occurring around pre-deformation slip bands, and subsequently leading to the formation of the bands with coarsened γ / γ ′ microstructure.

mechanisms.name: γ′ rafting
mechanisms.material_state: pre-deformed and annealed at 1100 °C for 5 h

evidence.quote: Introduction of tensile PD at room-temperature (RT) induces microstructure evolution similar to the γ ′ -rafting during HT in order to reduce internal elastic strain around the slip

mechanisms.name: creep pore formation
mechanisms.material_state: pre-deformed and annealed at 1100 °C for 5 h

evidence.quote: Such creep pores (so-called deformation pores or D-pores [ 28, 29 ]) already formed before the creep test. To be more specific, D-pores formed during the first stage of aging HT between 1100 – 1165 ◦ C.
